newsitem.title: UKRAINE: FOCUS-Ukraine, Italy to seek cash for super-highway.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Ukraine, Italy to seek cash for super-highway.

text.p: The prime ministers of Ukraine and Italy on Wednesday hailed growing bilateral trade and vowed to build a southern European transport corridor.

"The volume of bilateral trade has doubled since 1994 and reached almost $700 million last year," Ukrainian Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko told a news conference held with his Italian counterpart Romano Prodi.

"We will concentrate on links between small and medium businesses and enterprises, with the priority on training experts, on the agriculture sector and on investment," Lazarenko said, adding that there were 170 Ukrainian-Italian ventures.
The two prime ministers said Italy and Ukraine should find cash for a Triest-Ljubljana-Budapest-Kiev transport corridor.
The corridor has been built as far as Budapest and is expected to include a fast highway and railway.

"Italy, Slovenia, Hungary and Ukraine have so far expressed a strong wish to go ahead with this project. Without completing such a highway it would be impossible to develop normal economic relations between them," Prodi said.

"This is one of the most serious and difficult projects in the new Europe. The search for cash is going on with the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the World Bank to make sure this project is completed."

Roman Shpek, head of Ukraine's Agency for Reconstruction and Development, told Reuters there was no exact figure for required investment but both sides were "rather talking about the principles of financing".
"We have been proposing this idea for many many years but as before, we still have no money," Volodymyr Shtanov, deputy director of a state-funded transport think-tank said.
Other proposed projects outside southern Europe included an extension of the Berlin-Wroclaw highway to Ukraine's western city of Lviv and on to Kiev.
Official statements said Ukraine wanted eventually to extend the Triest-Kiev link to Kazakhstan and China.
Ukrainian has asked Prodi to speed up Italy's ratification of a 1994 cooperation treaty between Ukraine and the European Union, so far ratified only by six of the 15 EU members, officials say.
Prodi was due to meet President Leonid Kuchma later in the western Ukrainian city of Lviv, where the Ukrainian leader is on holiday.
